text:
alex_support: FYI customer reports svc.prod.acme.internal returning NXDOMAIN from their app hosts after yesterday's VPC peering update. 8:28am UTC

lina_sre: ack — can you paste a dig from one of their nodes and the same from our resolver?

alex_support: sure, asked them to run this: `dig +short svc.prod.acme.internal @169.254.169.253` (their node-local resolver). they sent back: ` `

alex_support: ```
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;svc.prod.acme.internal.   IN A
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
acme.internal.  300 IN SOA ns-1.route53.amazon.com. hostmaster.acme.internal. 1 7200 900 1209600 300
```

alex_support: but when i run a dig from our shared resolver (10.2.5.10) i get an A record.

ben_eng: interesting. that smells like a split-horizon / hosted zone association issue or node-local cache returning stale NXDOMAIN after VPC peering changes. did they recently re-associate hosted zones?

raj_platform: can we confirm whether the private hosted zone for acme.internal is associated with both VPCs (customer-prod-vpc and peered-tenant-vpc)? alex, can you ask for `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name acme.internal` and `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id <zoneid>` output?

alex_support: asked, customer replied with snippet: ```
$ aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name acme.internal
{
  "HostedZones": [
    {
      "Id": "/hostedzone/Z1ACMEEXAMPLE",
      "Name": "acme.internal.",
      "Config": { "PrivateZone": true }
    }
  ]
}
$ aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id /hostedzone/Z1ACMEEXAMPLE
{
  "VPCs": [
    { "VPCRegion": "us-west-2", "VPCId": "vpc-0a1b2c3d" }
  ]
}
```

alex_support: zone is only associated to vpc-0a1b2c3d (their old prod VPC). after peering we expected it to be associated to the peered/consumer VPC too.

lina_sre: that explains NXDOMAIN from nodes in the peered VPC. Route 53 private hosted zones only resolve for associated VPCs. Peering alone doesn't automatically associate.

ben_eng: additional wrinkle: we have node-local DNS caches (nodelocaldns) on their k8s nodes. if they queried right after the peering change and the node-local cache saw NXDOMAIN it might keep serving NXDOMAIN until TTL expiry. ask them to flush node-local cache or restart the kube-dns/nodelocaldns daemonset on an affected node.

raj_platform: steps for them to fix ASAP:
1) Associate the hosted zone with the peered VPC: `aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z1ACMEEXAMPLE --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0f9e8d7c`
2) On affected nodes, flush nodelocaldns cache or restart pods: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset nodelocaldns` (or `systemctl restart systemd-resolved` if they use host resolver)
3) Verify with `dig +short svc.prod.acme.internal @<node-local-ip>` and `dig +trace svc.prod.acme.internal`

alex_support: they've tried associate already but got `HostedZoneAlreadyAssociatedWithVPC` error for the target VPC id. they're sending the exact error now.

alex_support: error: `An error occurred (HostedZoneAlreadyAssociatedWithVPC) when calling the AssociateVPCWithHostedZone operation: The specified hosted zone is already associated with the specified VPC.`

lina_sre: odd: that suggests there may be a second hosted zone with the same name in another account or region causing confusion — or the API is reporting the VPC in another account identifier. request a full list of associations: `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z1ACMEEXAMPLE` (we already have) — verify the VPCIds and compare to the VPCId on the failing nodes via `curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/network/interfaces/macs/$(ip -o link show | awk '/eth0/{print $2}' | sed 's/:$//')/vpc-id` (if EC2).

ben_eng: also ask them to check for overlapping private hosted zones (same domain owned by another account) — Route53 can have multiple private zones with same name in different accounts; resolution depends on VPC associations and account; if peered VPCs live in different accounts, you must share the hosted zone or associate the VPC with the correct zone/account.

raj_platform: i'm going to check our side: infra-bot, any recent changes to resolver rules or egress allowlists that would block 53/UDP to route53 resolver endpoints?

infra-bot: noticed outbound 53 UDP to 10.0.0.2 (VPC resolver endpoint) was allowed. No recent rule changes in the last 48h.

lina_sre: additionally, confirm that the pods are not using a stubDomain that overrides acme.internal to point at a different resolver. `kubectl -n kube-system get configmap coredns -o yaml` and inspect `stubDomains`/`proxy` entries.

alex_support: customer ran `kubectl -n kube-system get configmap coredns -o yaml` and shows no stub for acme.internal.

ben_eng: request that they run these verification commands and attach outputs:
- `dig +short svc.prod.acme.internal @10.0.0.2` (VPC resolver)
- `dig +short svc.prod.acme.internal @169.254.169.253` (node-local)
- `aws ec2 describe-vpcs --vpc-ids vpc-0f9e8d7c --query 'Vpcs[].VpcId'`
- `kubectl -n kube-system logs daemonset/nodelocaldns` (one line tail)

alex_support: customer replied with new dig: `@10.0.0.2 -> 203.0.113.10` (correct), `@169.254.169.253 -> NXDOMAIN`. nodelocaldns logs show repeated NXDOMAIN cache hits for the fqdn.

lina_sre: so the fix path is clear: remove the stale NXDOMAIN cache (restart daemonset) and ensure the hosted zone association is present for the VPC where nodes live. if the customer cannot associate because of cross-account constraints, they can use Resource Access Manager (RAM) to share the hosted zone or create a dedicated zone in their account and sync records.

raj_platform: i'm going to create a short runbook snippet for support steps and post to docs later. quick temporary mitigation for them: restart nodelocaldns pods on a rolling basis — that will unstick the NXDOMAIN cache without affecting traffic significantly.

ben_eng: also remind them to check TTLs for SOA/negative caching (NXDOMAIN TTL / SOA minimum) — NXDOMAIN negative caching can be long depending on SOA settings.

alex_support: customer restarted nodelocaldns and now reports resolution fixed across nodes. they're going to follow up with their infra team on hosted zone association and RAM sharing.

lina_sre: great. can we keep this thread open until they confirm hosted zone association/perm fix?

alex_support: keeping open. i'll update when customer confirms. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident note created: INC-2026-3123456789 — marked as resolved (temporary) pending hosted zone association follow-up.
